baseline.reason: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; Root cause confirmed by source diff: in post_intro's h2645_sei_to_side_data(), for the Ambient Viewing Environment SEI, a new AVAmbientViewingEnvironment (dst_env) is allocated, wrapped in an AVBufferRef (buf), and buf is handed to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext() BEFORE dst_env's fields are written. ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext() (decode.c) unconditionally av_buffer_unref()s its buf argument once it decides not to add it (the side_data_pref() 'already exists, prefer existing' path, taken when the frame already has AV_FRAME_DATA_AMBIENT_VIEWING_ENVIRONMENT side data and side_data_pref_mask has that bit set), yet returns success (0) in that case. The caller's `if (ret < 0) return ret;` guard therefore does not fire, and code proceeds to write dst_env->ambient_illuminance/ambient_light_x/ambient_light_y into the just-freed buffer. In post_benign (the fix), the three field writes are moved to occur before the call to ff_frame_new_side_data_from_buf_ext(), so by the time the buffer can be freed the struct is already fully initialized and never written to again. In pre_intro (the code before the intro commit), this code path did not exist in this form at all (it used av_ambient_viewing_environment_create_side_data(frame) directly, with no separate buffer hand-off/free window). I verified this with a harness that directly drives the shared, exported ff_h2645_sei_to_frame() function (used identically by both the HEVC and H264 decoders once per decoded frame) with the precise state a real decode of a crafted mp4 would create (container-level 'amve' box side data already on the frame + side_data_prefer_packet=-1 + an Ambient Viewing Environment SEI in the bitstream). This drives the real compiled library code through its actual production entry point, reaching and executing the vulnerable statement; it is not a source-level assertion, grep, or unexecuted path. The identical command, run via run_poc, crashes only under post_intro and completes cleanly under both pre_intro and post_benign -- exactly the discriminating behavior required. A full end-to-end mp4-container-plus-valid-HEVC-bitstream PoC could not be produced in this environment (the sanitizer build has no software H.264/HEVC encoder configured, so no compliant bitstream could be authored via the ffmpeg CLI), so the harness reproduces the same code path via the library's own exported API instead.
